title: Breast cancer PDxO cultures for drug discovery and functional precision oncology
protocol: Harvest PDX tumor under aseptic conditions.
Add 5 mL of warm advanced DMEM/F12 media to a 10 cm tissue culture plate.
Transfer PDX tumor tissue to a plate.
Remove necrotic tissue areas from the PDX tumor tissue.
Cut healthy tumor tissue into 3 × 3 mm fragments.
Transfer tumor fragments into a C tube.
Digest tumor fragments in a GentleMACS Dissociator using human dissociation enzymes.
Assess digested material under the microscope.
Perform differential centrifugation to remove single cells if the digested material contains a mixture of organoids and single cells.
Embed organoids into a Matrigel dome after removing single cells by differential centrifugation.
Embed the material immediately if it contains only organoids.
Aggregate single cell-containing digestions for 16 hours on Ultra Low Attachment plates prior to embedding.
Place the plate on ice and keep cold for all following steps.
Place a paper towel directly onto the ice underneath the dish to keep it from moving.
Cut the tumor in half using two scalpels and look for white (necrotic) areas.
Carefully remove and discard the necrotic areas from the tissue.
Chop PDX tumor into 3 × 3 mm fragments in the dish using scalpels.
Add 5 mL warm advanced DMEM/F12 medium to GentleMACS C-tube.
Add 200 μL Enzyme H, 100 μL Enzyme R, and 25 μL Enzyme A to the C-tube.
Add 5 μL Y-27632 (10 nM working concentration) to the C-tube.
Transfer 10 PDX tumor fragments to C-tube using a cell lifter without transferring media.
Thaw the vial of tumor fragments in a 37°C water bath if cryopreserved PDX tissue is used.
Transfer fragments to a 10-cm tissue culture plate.
Aspirate freezing media and wash once with 5 mL advanced DMEM/F12.
Aspirate medium and transfer fragments to C-tube.
Close C-tube cap tightly.
Place C-tube onto GentleMACS Dissociator according to manufacturer’s instructions.
Place octoheaters over C-tube.
Run GentleMACS program “37C_h_TDK_3”.
Centrifuge (3 min, 300 × g, 20°C) to pellet digested tissue after running the program.
Carefully aspirate supernatant without disturbing the pellet.
Prepare a filter to attach to the tip of the aspirating pipet.
Incubate digested material with TAC buffer for 10 minutes at 37°C, shaking gently every 2–3 minutes if red blood cells are present.
Centrifuge the mixture for 3 minutes at 300 × g and 20°C.
Resuspend the pellet in 5 mL of warm PDxO base medium.
Place a 5 μL drop of digested material on a hemocytometer without cover glass.
Evaluate the contents of digested material under microscope to assess organoid size, health, and presence of single cells and debris.
Strain through a 200–500 μm cell strainer depending on organoid and debris size to remove larger debris and fat.
Wash C-tube and strainer with 10 mL PDxO medium.
Transfer flowthrough into a 15 mL conical tube.
Centrifuge the tube for 3 minutes at 300 × g at 20°C.
Resuspend the pellet in 5 mL of warm PDxO base medium.
Repeat the process, gradually decreasing the pore size of the strainer until most debris and fat are eliminated.
Place a 5 μL drop of digested material on the hemocytometer without cover glass.
Evaluate the contents under the microscope to determine the next steps.
Proceed with differential centrifugation if organoids and single cells are present in the digested material.
Resuspend organoid preparation in 15 mL of media for differential centrifugation (DC).
Perform initial centrifugation at 1 minute.
Discard supernatant and resuspend pellet.
Repeat centrifugation with shorter times: first at 40 seconds, then at 30 seconds.
Assess material under microscope after each spin to determine if further DC steps are necessary.
Proceed to counting and embedding of organoids if only organoids remain.
Incubate the plate for 5 min at 37°C.
Flip the plate upside down and place it back into the incubator for 10 min.
Add subtype-specific media to the well after incubation.
Aggregate single cells on an ultra-low adhesion plate for 16 h.
Embed the cells the following day.
If fewer than 50,000 cells are obtained in the pellet fraction after digestion, collect and spin down all single cells after digestion.
Incubate the collected single cells on a ultra low attachment (ULA) plate for 16 h.
Embed the next day in a scaled-down "mini-dome" using 100 μL of Matrigel:Cell mixture and a 25 μL Matrigel base layer in a 12-well plate.
Perform differential centrifugation to separate single cells from tumor cell aggregates or organoids.
Gently resuspend the pellet in 15 mL of warm PDxO base medium in a 15 mL conical tube.
Centrifuge at 300 × g for 1 min.
Transfer supernatant to another 15 mL conical tube.
Resuspend pellet in 5 mL of warm PDxO base medium.
Evaluate resuspended pellet and supernatant under microscope.
Fill up the conical tube containing the resuspended pellet to 15 mL with warm PDxO base medium.
Centrifuge at 300 × g for 50 seconds.
Transfer supernatant to another tube.
Resuspend pellet in 5 mL of warm PDxO base medium.
Evaluate resuspended pellet and supernatant under microscope.
Fill up the conical tube containing the resuspended pellet to 15 mL with warm PDxO base medium.
Centrifuge at 300 × g for 40 seconds.
Transfer supernatant to another tube.
Resuspend pellet in 5 mL of warm PDxO base medium.
Resuspend pellet and supernatant under microscope.
Fill up conical tube containing resuspended pellet to 15 mL of warm PDxO base medium.
Centrifuge at 300 × g for 30 seconds.
Transfer supernatant to another tube.
Resuspend pellet in 5 mL of warm PDxO base medium.
Evaluate resuspended pellet and supernatant under microscope.
Fill up conical tube containing resuspended pellet to 15 mL of warm PDxO base medium.
Centrifuge at 300 × g for 30 seconds.
Transfer supernatant to another tube.
Resuspend pellet in 5 mL of warm PDxO base medium.
Evaluate resuspended pellet and supernatant under microscope.
If organoid fraction is clean, proceed to the next step.
If not, repeat centrifugation at 300 × g for 30 seconds, monitoring compositions until a clean organoid fraction is achieved.
Drop 5 μL of digested material onto hemocytometer without cover glass.
Flick the hemocytometer gently with your finger.
Count all organoids in now spread out 5 μL drop using microscope.
Multiply organoid count by 200 and by total volume (mL) to calculate total number of organoids.
Pellet organoids by centrifugation at 300 x g for 3 minutes at 20°C.
Aspirate the supernatant from the pellets.
Resuspend the organoids in PDxO cryopreservation medium.
Transfer approximately 5,000 to 10,000 organoids or 0.5–1.0 × 10^6 cells per vial.
Load the vials into a Mr. Frosty container and place them at -80°C for 24 hours.
Transfer the vials to liquid nitrogen (LN2) for long-term storage after 24 hours.
Coat the center of each well in a 6-well plate with 50 μL Matrigel base layer.
Allow the Matrigel base layer to polymerize at 37°C for 5 minutes.
Resuspend 0.5–2 × 10^4 organoids per number of desired wells in 200 μl Matrigel on ice.
Calculate for 15%–20% more than needed when pipetting Matrigel.
Pipette gently 5-10 times to establish good distribution without destroying organoids and without introducing air bubbles.
Carefully add 200 μL of the organoids:Matrigel mixture onto each base layer.
Flip the plate upside down on its lid after 5 min at 37°C for Matrigel polymerization.
After indicated 15 min, flip the plate back over and add 5 mL fresh complete PDxO medium to each well.
Pipette media onto the side of the well.
Replace the complete PDxO medium every 3–4 days.
Aspirate the medium from matrigel:organoid dome.
Add 5 mL fresh complete PDxO medium specific to the breast cancer subtype of the PDxO.
Pellet cells by centrifugation (300 × g, 3 min, 20°C).
Aspirate supernatant.
Resuspend in PDxO medium with breast cancer subtype-specific supplements added.
Aim for 500,000–2,000,000 cells per each well of a 6 well plate.
Carefully pipette cells into a well of an ultra-low attachment (ULA) 6-well plate.
Place the plate in the incubator for 16-24 h at 37°C and 5% CO2.
Plate cells into a well of a 6-well ULA plate.
Incubate for 16 hours.
Pipette the medium and cell aggregates carefully.
Transfer the mixture into a 15 mL conical tube.
Centrifuge at 300 × g for 3 minutes at 20°C.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Embed the pellet in a Matrigel dome.
Change culture media every 3-4 days to allow PDxOs to grow.
Transfer leftover media containing PDX tumor fragments into a 15 mL conical tube.
Centrifuge samples for 5 minutes at 300 × g and 20°C.
Pellet cells by centrifugation.
Optionally, aggregate MDM cultures on ULA plates for 16 hours.
Embed aggregated MDM cultures the next day following step 27.
Strain PDxO cultures to start with single tumor cells or small clusters.
Start PDxO cultures by straining and immediately embedding.
Evaluate organoid health under a microscope before splitting.
Split PDxO cultures from passage 0 (P0) to P1 approximately 7-21 days after initial embedding.
Remove media from PDxOs once mature.
Add dispase solution to Matrigel domes containing PDxOs.
Break up Matrigel domes manually and incubate at 37°C.
Wash the organoids with media and centrifuge.
Resuspend the organoid pellet in TrypLE to disassociate PDxOs into single cells.
Assess the cells under a microscope, count them, and embed them in Matrigel.
Check PDxO health, density, and phenotype under the microscope.
Aspirate medium.
Add 1 mL freshly-made dispase solution to each well.
Tilt plate and use a cell scraper to scrape the dome into the dispase solution.
Carefully pipette (p1000) 5–10 times to break up Matrigel into smaller fragments.
Incubate 1 h at 37°C.
Check Matrigel digestion using a microscope.
Transfer to 15 mL conical tube.
Fill tube up to 15 mL with PDxO base medium.
Centrifuge (300 × g, 3 min, 20°C) to pellet organoids.
Aspirate supernatant.
Check the PDxO phenotype every 20 min during the 1 h dispase incubation step and move to the next step if PDxOs start to fall apart.
Resuspend organoid pellet in 2 ml TrypLE + 2 μL Y-27632.
Transfer suspension to a well of a new 6-well tissue culture plate.
Incubate at 37°C for 3–15 min until organoids are just dissociated.
Pipette (p1000) aggressively 15–20 times every 3-5 minutes and check organoid dissociation progress with a microscope.
As soon as organoids are dissociated, pipette up and down to mix and remove 10 μL for cell counting using an automated counter or hemocytometer.
Transfer dissociated organoids into a 15 ml conical tube.
Wash the well with PDxO base medium to increase cell recovery.
Fill the conical tube up to 15 ml with PDxO base medium and centrifuge at 300 × g for 3 min to pellet cells.
Embed the dissociated cells into new Matrigel domes following step 26.
Check organoid health, density, and phenotype using the microscope.
Tilt plate towards you and aspirate medium.
Add 2 mL TrypLE and 2 μL Y-27632 onto the dome.
Use a cell scraper to lift the dome off the plate so that it floats in the TrypLE solution.
Use a p1000 pipette to manually break up the dome by pipetting up and down 5–10 times.
Remove media from the well and discard.
Add 1 mL of freshly prepared PDxO cryopreservation medium to each well of mature organoids.
Tilt plate and use cell lifter to scrape Matrigel dome into bottom
Place cryovial into a 37°C water bath until just thawed.
Transfer contents to 15 mL conical and fill up with 13 mL warm PDxO base medium.
Centrifuge (300 × g, 3 min, 20°C).
Aspirate supernatant carefully to avoid aspirating organoids present in the cloudy Matrigel layer.
Repeat washing step if organoids are present in the cloudy Matrigel layer.
Embed into Matrigel domes right away following step 26.
Aspirate medium from PDxO cultures.
Add 1 mL freshly-made dispase solution to each well.
Tilt plate and use a cell scraper to scrape the dome into the dispase solution.
Pipette (p1000) 5-10 times to break up Matrigel into smaller fragments.
Incubate for 30 min - 1 h at 37°C.
Transfer to a 15 mL conical tube.
Fill the tube up to 15 mL with ice-cold non-supplemented Advanced DMEM/F12 medium.
Mix by inverting the conical tube multiple times.
Centrifuge (300 × g, 3 min, 4°C) to pellet organoids.
Aspirate supernatant from organoid pellet, ensuring not to remove the cloudy layer containing most organoids.
Add 2 mL ice-cold non-supplemented Advanced DMEM/F12 onto the pellet.
Pipette up and down 10 times with P1000.
Fill up to 15 mL with ice-cold non-supplemented Advanced DMEM/F12.
Mix tube and centrifuge at 300 × g for 3 minutes at 4°C.
Remove supernatant.
Resuspend pellet in 300 μL of RLT Plus Buffer with freshly added BME.
Transfer resuspended sample to a 1.5 mL microtube.
Vortex the sample at maximum speed for 1 minute.
Optional: Freeze and store the sample at −80°C.
If samples were stored at −80°C, thaw them in a 37°C water bath for 5 minutes.
Vortex the thawed sample at maximum speed for 1 minute.
Pipette RLT lysate onto QiaShredder spin column.
Centrifuge the QiaShredder spin column at maximum speed for 1 minute at 20°C.
Check column and centrifuge again if liquid is still visible on top of spin column.
Discard column. Transfer flow-through to AllPrep DNA binding column.
Centrifuge (10,000 × g, 30 s, 20°C).
Place AllPrep DNA binding column in a new collection tube and set on ice.
Save flow-through for RNA extraction.
Add 1 volume of 70% RNase-free molecular grade ethanol to flow-through.
Immediately mix by pipetting up and down with P1000.
Quickly transfer 600 μL of mixture onto AllPrep RNA binding column.
Centrifuge (10,000 × g, 15 s, 20°C), discard flow-through.
Transfer any remaining volume of sample to same column.
Centrifuge (10,000 × g, 15 s, 20°C), discard flow-through.
Add 350 μL RW1, centrifuge (10,000 × g, 15 s, 20°C), discard flow-through.
In a separate 1.5 mL tube mix 10 μL DNase I stock solution to 70 μL Buffer RDD and gently mix by pipetting.
Add 80 μL of DNase incubation mix directly onto the AllPrep RNA binding column.
Incubate for 15 min at 20°C.
Add 350 μL RW1, centrifuge (10,000 × g, 15 s, 20°C), discard flow-through.
Add 500 μL RPE.
Centrifuge at 10,000 × g for 15 seconds at 20°C.
Discard the flow-through.
Add 500 μL RPE.
Centrifuge at 10,000 × g for 2 minutes at 20°C.
Discard the flow-through.
Place the column in a new collection tube and dry spin at maximum speed for 1 minute at 20°C.
Place the column in a 1.5 mL microtube.
Add 30 μL of RNase-free water directly onto the column.
Centrifuge at 10,000 × g for 1 minute at 20°C to elute RNA.
Place the tube on ice and quantify RNA concentration using Qubit BR RNA Assay.
Remove DNA binding column from ice.
Add 500 μL AW1.
Centrifuge at 10,000 × g for 15 seconds at 20°C.
Discard the flow-through.
Add 500 μL AW2.
Centrifuge at maximum speed for 2 minutes at 20°C.
Discard the flow-through.
Place the column in a 1.5 mL microtube.
Add 100 μL of EB Buffer directly onto the column and incubate for 1 minute at 20°C.
Centrifuge at 10,000 × g for 1 minute at 20°C to elute DNA.
Place the tube on ice and quantify DNA concentration using Qubit BR dsDNA Assay.
Store RNA and DNA at -80°C.
Use 1 μL of extracted nucleic acids for the Qubit assay.
Requantify using high sensitivity (HS) Qubit kits if RNA or DNA concentrations are below 50 ng/μL.
Thaw vial in a 37°C water bath if using viably frozen cryostocks.
Transfer thawed sample to a 1.5 mL microtube and centrifuge at 300 × g for 3 minutes at 20°C.
Resuspend pellet in 300 μL of RLT Plus Buffer with freshly added BME and proceed with step 38.
Work quickly through the nucleic acid extraction protocol to ensure maximum yields.
Do not isolate RNA/DNA from more than 10 samples at once.
Utilize a kit for Short Tandem Repeats (STR) analysis which requires only a few ng of DNA as input for a PCR reaction.
Run fluorescent PCR products on a Genetic Analyzer or send off for analysis.
Use GeneWiz’s service for STR assay validation.
Compare results of matching patient-derived models like PDX and PDxOs to their original patient tumor.
Verify the origin of PDxOs using unique patterns of STRs.
Add 0.08 ng/μL DNA in a volume of 5 μL to a 96 well PCR plate.
Add 7.5 μL of Master Mix provided by the AmpFLSTR™ Identifiler™ Plus PCR Amplification Kit.
Use AmpFLSTR™ Identifiler™ Plus PCR Amplification Kit according to manufacturer’s protocol.
Analyze PCR product using genetic analyzer or Genewiz.
Compare unique patterns of STR peaks between samples.
Perform qRT-PCR to detect presence of mouse cells in PDxO culture.
Eliminate mouse cells from cultures if present.
Monitor residual mouse cells up to day 60 or passage 2 for self-elimination.
Identify persistent mouse cells if they do not eliminate by day 60 or passage 2.
In Matrigel, identify mouse cells with elongated phenotype and mesenchymal characteristics.

Prepare RNase-free water according to the manufacturer's recommendation using 8 μL final volume.
Use the same amount of RNA for each sample within one run.
Calculate and add per sample, plus 10% extra: 1 μL 10× ezDNase Buffer and 1 μL ezDNase enzyme. Mix well.
Add 2 μL of the ezDNase buffer mix to each sample into the first set of tubes from step 40b to get a final volume of 10 μL and mix well.
Incubate for 2 min at 37°C.
In a 1.5 mL microtube prepare IV VILO Solution: Calculate per sample, plus 10% extra: 4 μL IV VILO Master Mix and 6 μL nuclease-free water. Mix well.
Add 10 μL IV VILO Solution to tubes from step 40e and mix gently.
Start cDNA synthesis in thermal cycler using the program provided in the SuperScript IV Vilo kit data sheet.
For qRT-PCR, reconstitute mouse Gapdh F + R (forward + reverse) and human GAPDH F + R primers in IDT buffer as 40× stocks.
Calculate to use enough reaction mixture to run 1 ng of cDNA for each sample in a final volume of 5 μL, with each sample run in technical quadruplicates.
Account for a "no cDNA" sample in each run for negative control.
Add 2× PowerUp SYBR Green Master Mix to PCR tubes.
Calculate the volume needed to end up with 1 ng of cDNA per PCR tube and add it.
Mix well.
Dilute primers in a separate 1.5 mL tube for 500 nM primer of each forward and reverse primer per sample.
Pipette 15 μL of the cDNA/SYBR mixture from step into new PCR tubes.
Add 15 μL of diluted primer mixture to the PCR tubes.
Mix well.
Transfer 5 μL of reaction mix per well into a 384-well PCR plate in technical quadruplicates.
Cover the PCR plate with light cycler-compatible foil.
Spin the plate at 350 × g for 2 minutes at 20°C.

Run qRT-PCR on the light cycler using standard cycling mode: Denaturation for 2 min at 95°C, followed by 40 cycles of denaturation at 15 s at 95°C and elongation at 45 s at 60°C, then a melt curve from 65°C to 95°C at 0.5°C per minute.
Average the technical replicate CT values for analysis.
Subtract human GAPDH CT from mouse Gapdh CT to calculate ΔCT.
If desired, display ΔCT values as a heatmap.
Note: PDxO cultures with a mouse Gapdh CT of 32 or higher are considered "mouse free" for PDxO.
Eliminate mouse cells by FACS when PDxOs can be detected after an extended culture time (>200 days or 10 passages).
Perform one mouse cell elimination method (FACS or MCD) and embed the PDxOs.
Check the matured PDxO culture for mouse cell content again to determine if one elimination step was sufficient.
Use differential centrifugation as a short-term solution for eliminating mouse cells in PDxO cultures.
Culture PDxOs for 1–2 passages prior to FACS to ensure organoid outgrowth post-FACS is not impaired.
Purify PDxOs containing mouse cells by FACS once the cell number reaches ≥ 1 × 10^6 and is > P0.
Use a simple, pooled antibody 2-channel strategy for mouse cell elimination.
Remove media from well.
Add dispase solution and use cell lifter to dislodge dome from culture plate.
Use pipette to mechanically disrupt dome.
Incubate for 20–30 min at 37°C.
Transfer into a 15 mL conical tube and fill up to 15 ml with PDxO base media.
Optional: Perform differential centrifugation (300 × g, 30 or 40 s, 20°C).
Aspirate supernatant and continue with TrypLE step on the pellet.
Centrifuge (300 × g, 3 min, 20°C).
Aspirate and discard supernatant.
Resuspend cells in cold FACS buffer at a concentration of 1.0 × 10^6 cells/mL.
Add Y-27632 (at a ratio of 1:1000) and transfer into a 5 mL conical tube.

Transfer to an FACS tube and keep on ice until flow sorting.
Sort human cells into a 15 mL conical tube containing 5 mL complete PDxO media.
Sort human cells immediately after staining.

Resuspend the cells in 5 mL complete PDxO media.

Transfer aggregates into a 15 mL conical tube without washing the plate.

Embed the cells into Matrigel dome following step 26.

Remove media from well.
Add dispase solution and use cell lifter to dislodge dome from culture plate.

Prepare PDxOs suspensions and plate them onto the base layers in 384-well plates.
Prepare at least two plates per drug testing assay: one screening plate and one day 0 plate.
On the next day, prepare drug dilutions for the screening plate.
Add drugs to the screening plate on the same day as preparation.
Perform CTG3D assay on the day 0 plate to generate baseline readings.
At day 6, perform CTG3D assay on the screening plate.
Wait at least two passages for PDxOs to ensure stable growth rate.
Check PDxO health, density, and phenotype by microscope.
Prepare one dome of organoids that have reached an average size of at least 50 μm up to 100 μm per well.
Disassociate the dome by aspirating media and incubating in dispase for 20–30 minutes.
Coat plates with EHS matrix.
Chill 384-well plates for 1 hour at 4°C.
Put plates on ice and keep cool during all steps.
Pre-chill a 150 mL reservoir by stacking it onto a 300 mL reservoir filled with ice.
Calculate the total volume needed for 10 μL of EHS-derived matrix per well.
Fill the EHS-derived matrix into the 150 mL reservoir and keep cool.
Deposit 10 μL of EHS-derived matrix as a base layer into each well using a ViaFlo 96 or a 12 channel electronic repeater.
Spin the plates at 1200 × g for 1 minute at 4°C to ensure even distribution of EHS-derived matrix.
Prepare an extra 384-well plate with EHS matrix coating for measuring PDxO metabolic activity prior to drug treatment.
Incubate plates at 37°C for 10 min to 1 hour.
If plates will not be used within 1 hour, keep on ice and then incubate at 37°C for 10 minutes prior to use.
Transfer dissociated organoids into a 15 mL conical tube.
Fill the conical tube up to 15 mL with PDxO base medium.
Centrifuge at 300 × g for 3 minutes to pellet cells.
Discard supernatant and resuspend pellet with 15 mL of PDxO base medium.
Centrifuge at 300 × g for 3 minutes to pellet cells.
Plate PDxOs onto one well of a ULA 6-well plate in 5 mL PDxO complete media.
Incubate the plate at 37°C until plating is required.
Count the organoids by gently pipetting up and down with a P1000.
Remove 5 μL from the solution and drop onto a hemacytometer without adding a cover glass.
Under the microscope, count all organoids in the 5 μL drop.
Multiply the organoid count by 200 and by the total volume (mL) to calculate the total number of organoids.
Prepare a plating media mix as follows: Mix 700 μL EHS-derived matrix (5% v/v) with 14 μL Y-27632 and 13.3 mL cold PDxO base medium, keeping on ice.
Resuspend organoid pellet in 1 ml of PDxO base media.
Add the plating media mix to resuspended organoids.
Pipette volume needed to achieve a total number of 23–39,000 organoids into a 15 mL conical tube for plating.
Remove 384-well plate with Matrigel base layer from incubator.
Mix and transfer 14 mL plating master mix containing organoids to a 25 mL reservoir, on ice.
Mix organoid master mix in reservoir gently but thoroughly using an E1 12 channel electronic repeater pipette set to mix 300 μL, 3×, and max speed (10) in between dispenses.
Immediately after mixing, plate 30 μL master plating mix per well in 384-well plates onto matrix base layer using an E1 12 channel electronic repeater pipette set to 8×, 30 μL.
From remaining organoid master mix, plate 16 wells (30 μL/well) into a 384-well “day 0” plate using the same mixing/plating technique as above.
Incubate all 384 well plates at 37°C for 16 h.
Add 30 μL of warm PDxO base medium to each well using an E1 12 channel electronic repeater pipette.
Add 15 μL of CTG3D to each well using an E1 12 channel electronic repeater pipette or ViaFlo 96 liquid handler if > 5 plates are prepared.
Shake for 20 min at 500 rpm in the dark.
Read luminescence signal on plate reader.
Prepare drug stocks to 20 mM in DMSO according to manufacturer specifications.
Add 4 × 30 μl of PDxO base media (with additives) to rows G-A per screening plate.
Calculate and add ((4 × 30) × fold dilution factor) μl of PDxO base media (with additives) to row H per screening plate.
Determine the appropriate amount of a 20 mM drug stock solution needed per column to reach double the desired initial concentration, and add it to row H.
Mix by pipetting at least half the volume of the well three times in row H.
Dilute by chosen fold factor from rows H-A.
Include a vehicle control for each solvent used for drug dilutions.
Add 30 μL of drug solution to each well using a ViaFlo 96 liquid handler.
Incubate 384 well plates at 37°C for 6 days as a single layer, do not stack plates.
Remove seals from plates and add 15 μL of CTG3D to each well with ViaFlo 96.
Shake for 20 min at 500 rpm in the dark.
Read luminescence signal on plate reader (Envision).
